tr.td: MRI of the brain in the hospital: acute 12 mm lacunar infarct in the right internal capsule and corona radiata; chronic small-vessel white-matter changes in both hemispheres; no hemorrhage
CT angiography of the head and neck in the hospital: no carotid, vertebral, or intracranial stenosis or occlusion
Transthoracic echocardiography with bubble study in the hospital: normal left ventricular size and function, mild left ventricular hypertrophy, normal left atrium, no thrombus, no shunt
12-lead electrocardiogram: sinus rhythm 72/min, left ventricular hypertrophy by voltage, no atrial fibrillation
30-day ambulatory ECG monitoring: sinus rhythm throughout, occasional atrial ectopic beats, no atrial fibrillation or flutter
Outpatient physical and occupational therapy for left-sided weakness and hand dexterity, twice weekly, completed
Respiratory syncytial virus vaccine, single dose
Recombinant zoster vaccine, two-dose series completed

text.paragraph: Historical biography with true dates. These events are not part of the synthetic care timeline.

tr.td: Chest pain at the White House after straining to open a window; read at the time as a heart attack, but no heart disease was found and the episode was probably musculoskeletal (disputed)
Critical pneumonia in Tunis, treated with sulfonamides
First stroke, a less serious attack at Cap d'Ail described as spasm of a small artery
Further cerebrovascular episodes, including transient ischemic attacks, from 1950 to 1952
Stroke at a dinner at 10 Downing Street: left hemiparesis with a drooping mouth and slurred speech, worst on the third day; kept secret at the time

tr.td: Primary care transition visit eight days after a minor ischemic stroke
Two-week stroke review at the end of dual antiplatelet therapy, and neurology consultation
Eight-week stroke and blood pressure review with lipid panel and rhythm-monitor results
Three-month stroke review before returning to public speaking
Same-day sick visit for lightheadedness on standing
Aspirin with clopidogrel for 21 days after the minor stroke, then clopidogrel 75 mg alone
Atorvastatin 80 mg with a lipid panel 4 to 12 weeks after starting, aiming for LDL cholesterol below 70 mg/dL
Lower blood pressure below 130/80 with amlodipine and lisinopril, checking standing blood pressure at each visit and a basic metabolic panel 1 to 2 weeks after starting lisinopril

Neurology consultation to confirm the stroke mechanism, set the antiplatelet plan after the 21-day course, decide on prolonged cardiac rhythm monitoring, and advise on return to work and public speaking
Outpatient physical and occupational therapy for left-sided weakness, with fall-risk review at every visit
PHQ-9 at the first visit and at each review while symptoms persist, MoCA again within the first year, and attention to post-stroke tearfulness
Brief interventions at every visit for unhealthy alcohol use (AUDIT-C, no more than two drinks a day) and cigar smoking, with nicotine replacement offered
Yearly influenza vaccine and current COVID-19 vaccine
Lower blood pressure below 130/80 mmHg without orthostatic symptoms by the eight-week review
Blood pressure 128/76 mmHg on amlodipine 5 mg and lisinopril 5 mg; no orthostatic fall
Lower LDL cholesterol below 70 mg/dL by the eight-week review
LDL cholesterol 58 mg/dL on atorvastatin 80 mg
Return to full work and public speaking by about three months after the stroke
Back at full work; modified Rankin Scale 1
Keep to no more than two drinks on any day
AUDIT-C from 8 to 5; no longer drinking six or more on one occasion, but still above two drinks on some days
Cut down to three cigars a day as a step toward stopping
Three cigars a day; not ready to stop
